name: BabyIAXO
summary: An intermediate-scale IAXO instrument that validates subsystems while providing an independent solar-axion search capability.
detection_principle: A Sun-tracking magnet converts axions to X-rays, read out by two focusing-optics and low-background detection chains.

status.label: Under construction
status.evidence: Zaragoza CAPA's official page reports DFG approval of magnet-construction funding; the magnet is intended for BabyIAXO at DESY.

timeline.event: Conceptual Design of BabyIAXO, the intermediate stage towards the International Axion Observatory

collaboration.name: BabyIAXO Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: Conceptual design
key_parameters.value: Two magnet bores, each 10 m long and 70 cm in diameter

key_parameters.name: Projected sensitivity
key_parameters.value: g_aγ approximately 1.5×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹; mass reach can extend to approximately 0.25 eV

results.summary: The conceptual design sets detection targets; official 2026 updates show funding for the key magnet, rather than the start of solar data-taking.

science_scope: Primarily searches for solar-produced axions or hidden photons as complementary tests of dark-matter candidates. Solar flux is distinct from cold Galactic-halo dark matter; a solar-axion discovery alone would not establish the composition of cosmic dark matter.
